Biochemistry Ph.D. overview
Our interdisciplinary biochemistry Ph.D. program, which includes biology, biochemistry and biomedicine, gives you opportunities to complete basic or translational research in areas from cancer, infectious disease and neuroscience to immunology, cell signaling and developmental biology. You'll use a wide variety of techniques to explore a spectrum of important biological questions through innovative, collaborative and interdisciplinary approaches.

Why This Program Program Highlights Careers & Outcomes
Earning a biochemistry Ph.D.
Our biochemistry Ph.D. program will fuel your passion for research. Work with experienced and dedicated faculty advisors to explore a spectrum of important biological questions. Our researchers investigate topics including:
Cancer.
Infectious diseases.
Neuroscience.
Stress and aging.
Developmental biology.
Cytoskeleton and membrane trafficking.
Cell signaling.
Optogenetics.
You’ll be supported by a collaborative research environment including open-concept research labs, core facilities and specialty labs, such as our microscopy facility, and flow cytometry, insectary and radioisotope labs.
Your program will be individually tailored to emphasize professional skills and career development. You will work closely and regularly with your advisor and a committee of faculty to identify a personalized program of elective courses and create and cultivate an individual development plan.

Ph.D. program highlights
As a graduate student at CMU in the biochemistry Ph.D. program, you’ll:
Work with experts in their field: Be supported by dedicated faculty mentors who have demonstrated excellence in research and teaching and are committed to student success.
Create close personal and professional connections: Be part of a small and select program, ensuring that you receive significant interactions with faculty mentors.
Careers for a biochemistry Ph.D.
Students graduating with a biochemistry Ph.D. typically go into careers in academia, industry or other fields that draw on the knowledge and skills acquired during their graduate work.
